projects.name: Voice agents on ElevenLabs, with an MCP tool server
projects.oneLine: Seconds before a call ends, my dental agent calls a tool on my MCP server that writes the call’s state to the database, so the dental app shows it before the caller hangs up.

families.name: Dental front-desk agents
families.text: Inbound and outbound calls: schedule, cancel and reschedule appointments; answer questions about providers, doctors and general website enquiries; lead conversion and lead management for dental patients.

families.name: Insurance-verification agent
families.text: Speaks with insurance-provider representatives to collect the dental codes the existing RPA bot flow misses, and writes them to the database through MCP. Paired with the existing application by database polling on call creation, so the existing flow was not broken.

built: 15 ElevenLabs voice agents across two workspaces, in three families; 10 have logged usage.
Branching workflows of 9 to 10 nodes, with the LLM for each node chosen by task difficulty; up to about 50 versions on one agent.

The MCP-over-SSE tool server, built alone (91 of 113 commits): Bun and Express with a React front end, 11 SQL-backed tools (patients, appointments, availability, eligibility), on Azure App Service, shared by agents in two workspaces.
Multi-provider LLM orchestration across Groq, Azure OpenAI and Gemini, with live failover under rate limits.
Multilingual support with knowledge attached to the model; graceful and abrupt call endings handled.
checked: Test-driven development, a bug tracker and ordered SQL migrations on the tool server.
I read waterfall traces in Arize Phoenix to debug the agents.
I adapted the agents to ElevenLabs feature releases as they shipped, by trial and error.

projects.name: Azure Voice Live API prototype, GPT Realtime and an MCP tool server
projects.oneLine: A local real-time voice gateway on Azure's Voice Live API, wired to a stdio MCP server so the model can call dental-eligibility tools mid-conversation.
built: A Node.js WebSocket gateway and a React 19 browser client, connected to Azure AI Foundry's Voice Live API (GPT Realtime, Azure Neural TTS) over a persistent socket.
A telephony-codec transport adapter resampling 8kHz G.711 mu-law audio to 24kHz PCM16, so the same gateway can sit behind a phone call or a browser tab.
A stdio JSON-RPC MCP server exposing five dental-eligibility tools, wired into the realtime session as live function calls.
checked: Verified the WebSocket upgrade and audio round-trip against two realtime models, with server-side voice-activity detection tuned for natural turn-taking.
Measured under 100ms from user barge-in to playback purge, and exercised live MCP tool round-trips end to end.
Logged the gaps between this prototype and a production rollout in the repo's own docs, instead of presenting it as shipped.
notClaimed: This is a local prototype, not a deployed production system.
No call volume or user-facing deployment is claimed.

projects.name: Post-call audio analytics, scored by Claude Sonnet on Azure AI Foundry
projects.oneLine: A pipeline that turns a recorded coaching call into a scored, interactive report: audio in, a structured 14-metric Claude Sonnet assessment out.
built: A skill-coach voice agent built for dental front-desk role-play, reusing the post-call reporting pattern proven on earlier interview-assessment work.
A pipeline that pulls a call's transcript and recording, optionally diarizes it by speaker, and passes it to Claude Sonnet on Azure AI Foundry to score 14 metrics across three strictness modes.
A deterministic template engine that renders the scored result into a multi-tab interactive HTML report, instead of asking the model to emit the full report markup itself.
checked: Hit and fixed a real Azure AI Foundry issue where reasoning consumed the entire completion budget and returned empty text; fixed with an explicit thinking-budget setting and backoff on rate limits.
Confirmed by direct test that asking the model to emit the full 1,390-line HTML report in one completion was unreliable, which is why the report is templated, not model-generated.
Handed off as a small, dependency-free backend module, reusing a pattern proven on an earlier reporting pipeline.
notClaimed: This is a coaching and assessment tool, not a clinical or compliance system.
No accuracy or adoption figures beyond the engineering facts above are claimed.

projects.name: SafeSupport
projects.oneLine: A support-triage agent over real customer-support conversations, with an evaluation harness. Bulk labels wait for human sign-off.
built: Intent classification, a retrieval-grounded draft reply, and a decision to auto-handle or escalate.
An evaluation harness with baselines and ablations; 123 passing tests.
checked: In data prep I rejected mid-thread fragments: 24,253 of 106,860 brand replies, about 23%.
Bulk labelling waits for explicit human sign-off, because golden labels cannot come from the model class being evaluated.
notClaimed: No accuracy figure is quoted here; the evaluation is in the repo.
